q: Does the QSVC/ZFeatureMap headline (F1 ~ 0.98) survive on the true Kaggle ealaxi/banksim1 file at the natural imbalance ratio (~1.2% fraud), and is precision-at-recall=0.90 still competitive with a tuned XGBoost / Random Forest baseline?
basis: This replication used a synthetic BankSim-like 200-record balanced slice because Kaggle API access was unavailable. Paper itself uses a hand-balanced 100/100 subset that erases real-world imbalance. On imbalanced data, F1 collapses and PR-AUC becomes the honest metric; neither paper nor this replication reports PR-AUC.
next_steps: Obtain Kaggle token, pull ealaxi/banksim1 (~600K rows), rerun the exact 6-cell QSVC/VQC grid at (a) the paper's balanced 100/100 protocol for direct comparison and (b) natural imbalance with stratified sampling, reporting PR-AUC and precision at recall=0.90. Add XGBoost + RandomForest baselines. Wall-time budget on a single CPU: ~2 hours for QSVC (grows quadratically with n_train for FidelityQuantumKernel); use a 2000-record subsample if the full BankSim exceeds the kernel budget.

q: Does the QSVC/ZFeatureMap winner survive shot noise and depolarising noise, or is the reported F1 = 0.98 a statevector-simulator artifact?
basis: Paper uses Aer QasmSimulator (Sec. IV.B); in qiskit-ml 0.9, FidelityQuantumKernel defaults to the reference Sampler, which under our qiskit-aer 0.17 install is effectively statevector unless shots are set. A quantum-kernel result that vanishes under 1000-shot sampling or 0.5% two-qubit depolarising error is not deployable.
next_steps: Rerun QSVC/Z on Aer with (i) shots in {512, 1024, 4096, 16384, statevector-inf}, and (ii) a FakeManila / FakeMumbai noise model at scale factors {0.5x, 1x, 2x} device error. Plot F1 vs. shots and F1 vs. noise-scale. Also try a Sampler with the Estimator-Fidelity primitive from qiskit-ml 0.9 vs. the ComputeUncompute default. Free endpoint: local Aer, no cost.

q: Is the 4-feature choice (age, gender, category, amount) optimal, or would ML-driven feature-map selection (e.g., quantum-kernel-target-alignment or NISQ-friendly circuit search) find a better feature set or a better feature map than the three hand-picked (Z, ZZ, Pauli) ones?
basis: Paper's feature choice is by PCA + correlation heatmap inspection (Sec. III.B); the feature-map choice is by hand from three canonical ones. Both are ad-hoc. Recent work (Hubregtsen et al. 2022, Glick et al. 2024) shows kernel-target-alignment optimisation of the entangler pattern can shift QSVC F1 by 0.05-0.15 on comparable small datasets.
next_steps: Sweep entangler patterns for ZZFeatureMap (linear / circular / full / pairwise) at reps in {1,2,3}, score each by kernel-target alignment on the training split, then evaluate the top-3 aligned configs on the test split. Also try feature-subset ablations (all 6-choose-k for k in {3,4,5}) to see whether the 4-feature choice actually dominates. Runtime: ~30 min per ansatz on CPU.

q: Does the QSVC/ZFeatureMap advantage transfer to modern quantum-kernel methods (projected quantum kernels, Havlicek-style embedding + trainable ansatz) or to variational quantum kernels with learnable data-encoding scales?
basis: The paper compares three fixed feature maps only. Since 2023, projected quantum kernels (Huang et al. 2021) and trainable data-encoding kernels (Lloyd et al. 2020, Glick 2024) have become the honest state of the art for small-data quantum classifiers. A REPLICATED result on a superseded kernel family is a data point but not a competitiveness claim.
next_steps: Implement (a) a projected quantum kernel with projection dimension in {2, 4, 8} on the same 200-record BankSim slice, (b) a trainable data-scaling variant of ZFeatureMap where each rotation angle is multiplied by a learnable scalar, optimised jointly with the SVM margin. Compare F1 to QSVC/Z baseline. Free endpoint: local Aer or a Sophia H100 for JIT-compiled statevector sim.

q: Does the QML approach specialise usefully to any specific fraud subtype (card-not-present vs. card-present, merchant-category-specific, first-time-buyer vs. repeat), or is the balanced 100/100 evaluation hiding sharp per-subtype performance cliffs?
basis: Paper reports one aggregate F1 per (model, feature-map) cell. Real fraud detection needs per-segment performance because losses are dominated by a few high-value fraud subtypes. The balanced-subset design makes segment analysis impossible on the paper's slice.
next_steps: On the full BankSim file, stratify by (a) merchant category (10 categories, e.g., es_health, es_sportsandtoys, es_travel), (b) transaction amount decile, (c) customer age bucket. Report QSVC/Z F1 and PR-AUC per stratum vs. the classical baseline. Identify subtypes where quantum (if any) actually wins by more than 2 sigma of the seed distribution. Requires a 20-seed sweep for the sigma estimate; budget ~10 hours on CPU.
